title: Provisioning: add retry/backoff + safe cancellation for Imaging/Bootstrapping stages
author: Gabe Wilson
release_notes: Provisioning runs now use bounded retries with exponential backoff (+ jitter) for Imaging and Bootstrapping, and support safe cancellation without leaving duplicate in-flight work.
description:
Context: During staging pilot we saw runs get stuck or flap in Imaging/Bootstrapping due to transient infra/API errors (image fetch slowness, helm timeouts, occasional cloud rate limits). Operators were re-triggering runs, which occasionally produced duplicate work (e.g., overlapping bootstrap actions) or left ambiguous state. This PR implements a consistent retry/backoff policy for Imaging + Bootstrapping in the fleet provisioner, ensures cancellation is safe/observable, and prevents duplicate stage execution for a given pool.

What changed: (1) Added a bounded retry loop with exponential backoff + full jitter for Imaging and Bootstrapping. Defaults: maxAttempts=5, baseDelay=10s, maxDelay=5m. Retryability is driven by error categorization (timeouts, 429/5xx from upstream APIs, known transient SSH/agent-not-ready cases). Non-retryable errors (invalid config, authz/permission denied, explicit policy failures) fail fast and surface a clear operator-facing message. (2) Introduced a per-(pool_id, stage) execution lease to avoid duplicate work when multiple runs are triggered (human or automation). The lease is acquired before stage execution and renewed via heartbeat; if a second run arrives it will either (a) wait behind the current lease until it completes, or (b) fail with a deterministic “stage already in progress” error depending on the caller’s mode (default is wait with bounded timeout). (3) Implemented safe cancellation semantics: cancelling a run marks the run as CancelRequested, stops scheduling further attempts, and on next heartbeat boundary the in-progress worker exits cleanly. We do not attempt to “kill” external processes mid-flight; instead we ensure no further side effects are initiated and the lease is released promptly. The run transitions to Canceled with an audit log entry including who/what canceled and the last completed substep. (4) Added idempotency guards around side-effecting bootstrap operations. For helm applies we persist an execution token and require it to match the active lease; re-entrant calls become no-ops. For node labeling/registration writes we switched to upsert-by-node-id and made operations conditional on desired state to avoid repeated churn.

Operator impact: The CLI/status endpoint will now show attempt counts (e.g., Bootstrapping attempt 2/5), next retry ETA, and a normalized error category. If a stage is already running, operators will see a single linkable error message with the run_id holding the lease.

Why this is safe: (a) Retries are bounded and stage-scoped; we do not retry terminal validation/policy failures. (b) Leases guarantee at-most-one active Imaging/Bootstrapping executor per pool, even if multiple triggers are fired. (c) Cancellation is explicit and auditable, and prevents new side effects while allowing in-flight work to finish a safe boundary.

Testing: Added unit tests for retry categorization/backoff (incl. jitter bounds), lease acquisition/renewal/release, and cancellation transitions. Added integration-style tests with failure injection: simulated helm timeout then success; simulated repeated 429s then terminal; simulated concurrent triggers; simulated cancel mid-backoff and cancel during active lease. Also verified event emission: stage_attempt_started/failed/scheduled and run_canceled.

Rollout plan: This will ship behind the existing provisioning pipeline feature flag. We will enable in staging first and watch (1) stuck-stage alerts, (2) retry counts per stage, and (3) duplicate stage execution metrics (should drop to ~0). If retry loops cause prolonged time-to-ready, we can tune maxAttempts/maxDelay via config without redeploy.

Follow-ups: We likely want the same lease + retry contract applied to Validating once we have more data, but keeping scope limited here to the historically flaky stages (Imaging + Bootstrapping).

review_conversation: Rafael Mendes: Can we confirm we won’t retry on config/schema failures? We’ve seen retries hide real errors and inflate time-to-ready.

Gabe Wilson (author): Yep—categorization is explicit. Validation/policy failures are NonRetryableError and fail fast; retries only for transient infra/upstream categories (timeouts/429/5xx, agent-not-ready). Added tests to prevent regression.
Vanessa Ortiz: Lease semantics look good. Question: what happens if a worker dies without releasing the lease? Do we have TTL / takeover?

Gabe Wilson (author): Lease has (lease_expires_at) and requires heartbeat renewal every 30s. If worker dies, lease expires after 2m and next attempt/run can acquire. Also emits a “lease_expired” event so we can alert if it happens frequently.
Ethan Park: Please make sure cancel doesn’t leave the run stuck in an intermediate state. Do we always emit a terminal state and event?

Gabe Wilson (author): CancelRequested is treated as terminal-intent; scheduler stops scheduling new attempts immediately. Worker checks cancel flag at heartbeat boundaries and transitions to Canceled with an event. Added integration tests for cancel during backoff and cancel during active stage execution.
Nina Petrova: The bootstrap idempotency token—where is it stored and can it collide across runs?

Gabe Wilson (author): Stored with (pool_id, stage, active_run_id) and compared against the active lease/run id. Tokens are UUIDv4; collision is effectively impossible. It’s primarily to guard against re-entrant bootstrap calls and replay.
Rafael Mendes: Requesting one change: cap total time spent retrying so SRE paging doesn’t get delayed forever.
Gabe Wilson (author): Added stage-level maxElapsed=20m (configurable). Once exceeded, we fail with category=RetryBudgetExceeded. Pushed in follow-up commit.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved after maxElapsed change. Please link this in the runbook follow-up.
Gabe Wilson (author): Will do—added a short note in operator-notes.md and will reference in the provisioning runbook PR.
